roles.name: Account Manager
roles.summary: Owns existing customer accounts after the sale: renewals worked from 120 days out, expansion from usage and seat growth, and renewal paperwork ready for a person to price. It sends and signs nothing on its own.
roles.when: A team with recurring contracts whose renewals are handled in the last week and whose expansion depends on the customer asking.
pains: renewal quotes go out late or at last year's terms
we never ask happy customers to buy more
customers use more seats than they pay for
nobody owns the account once the deal closes
roles.first_routine: Weekly renewal and expansion review · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Accounts Payable Specialist
roles.summary: Gets every bill paid once, on time and to the right account. Each bill is logged, matched to its order or contract, and checked for duplicates and changed bank details. It proposes the weekly payment run and pays only requested, matched lines with verified details.
roles.when: A team that pays more than a handful of vendor bills a month, or has ever paid one twice, late, or to the wrong account.
pains: we paid the same bill twice
bills sit in someone's inbox until the late notice arrives
a vendor asked us to change its bank details by email
nobody knows what we owe vendors this month
late fees on bills we meant to pay
roles.first_routine: Weekly payment run proposal · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Accounts Receivable Specialist
roles.summary: Gets overdue invoices paid. Every week it reads the aging report, summarises it, and drafts a reminder for each overdue invoice, friendly first and firmer later, after checking for disputes and payments. A reminder goes out only when the task asks for it and mail sending is on.
roles.when: A team that invoices customers on terms and finds itself chasing payments late or not at all.
pains: customers pay invoices late and nobody chases them
we forget to follow up on overdue invoices
chasing payments feels awkward
cash is tight because customers pay slowly
we can't see which invoices are overdue
roles.first_routine: Weekly receivables reminders · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Benefits Administrator
roles.summary: Keeps benefits administration on time: the enrollment calendar, every joiner, leaver and life event tracked to its deadline, and plain-language plan comparisons. It never enrolls anyone, changes coverage or tells a person which plan to pick.
roles.when: A team that offers health or other benefits through a broker or provider and handles enrollment and changes by hand.
pains: open enrollment deadlines catch us out
a new hire's benefits start late
nobody can explain our plans in plain words
life event changes get missed
roles.first_routine: Weekly benefits deadlines · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Billing Specialist
roles.summary: Gets every invoice out on time and right the first time. Each invoice is built from the signed contract, the usage or the hours, and checked against terms, PO numbers and tax before it goes. It issues a requested, checked batch when its Tools allow, and customer messages stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico.
roles.when: A team that invoices customers from contracts, timesheets or usage, and loses days or payments to invoices that go out late or wrong.
pains: invoices go out late every month
customers send invoices back because the PO number is missing
we bill the wrong amount and have to credit it
we forgot to bill for work we delivered
roles.first_routine: Invoice run check · The 25th of each month at 09:00 team time, ahead of month-end invoicing

roles.name: Investor Relations Manager
roles.summary: Keeps investors informed. Each month it writes the investor update from goals, KPI readings and the finance figures a human supplies: metrics first, asks second, a short honest recap last. Every figure is checked and sourced. Messages to outsiders stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico, and no figure is invented.
roles.when: A team with investors or a board that expects a regular written update.
pains: writing the monthly investor update takes a day
we skip investor updates when things get busy
investors ask for numbers we scramble to find
board members ask what happened this month
roles.first_routine: Monthly investor update draft · The third of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: BotOps
roles.summary: The engineer that sets up every other bot from the templates and keeps their repositories, instructions and readiness working.

roles.name: Brand Manager
roles.summary: Keeps the brand rules written down, reviews copy and assets against them, checks new names, and audits what went public each month with three fixes. It changes no live page or asset itself.
roles.when: A team whose website, emails, decks and posts no longer sound or look like one team, or that is naming a new product.
pains: every team describes our team differently
our logo and colours are used wrong
new copy never sounds like us
we have no brand guidelines anyone follows
roles.first_routine: Monthly brand consistency audit · The 1st of each month at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Chief of Staff
roles.summary: Turns the goals, tasks, bot updates and meetings already in Tico into a weekly brief for the owner, chases stalled goals, and drafts Monday's agenda. Internal only.
pains: I don't know what is really going on across the team
goals stall and nobody notices
the Monday meeting has no agenda
things I asked for fall through the cracks
status updates take hours to compile
roles.first_routine: Weekly team brief · Fridays at 15:00 team time

roles.name: Community Manager
roles.summary: Keeps the customer community answered and alive: finds unanswered questions, prepares sourced replies, spots champions and routes feedback in one weekly digest. Public replies stay drafts until a person turns sending on.
roles.when: A team with a customer forum, Slack or Discord community, or user group where questions wait and the most helpful members go unthanked.
pains: questions in our community go unanswered for days
our customer forum has gone quiet
we don't know who our most helpful customers are
feedback posted in the community never reaches the product team
roles.first_routine: Weekly community digest · Fridays at 11:00 team time

roles.name: Compensation Analyst
roles.summary: Keeps pay consistent and defensible: salary bands per role and level, a check of every offer and pay change against its band, pay ranges for job posts, the annual review pack, and pay equity checks by group. Confidential; it never sets anyone's pay.
roles.when: A team of 25 or more that negotiates every offer from scratch, has to publish pay ranges, or wants to know its pay is fair before someone asks.
pains: every offer is negotiated from scratch
we don't know if we pay people fairly
job posts now need a pay range and we have none
the annual raise round is a spreadsheet mess
roles.first_routine: Weekly offer and pay change check · Wednesdays at 11:00 team time

roles.name: Compliance Manager
roles.summary: Keeps the compliance calendar: annual reports, licences, registered agent, regulatory filings and insurance renewals, each with an owner and proof it was done. Summaries for a human, not legal advice.
roles.when: A team registered in more than one place, holding licences or permits, or in a regulated trade, where a missed filing means a fine or a lapsed licence.
pains: we missed a state filing and paid a late fee
our business licence lapsed and nobody noticed
nobody knows which registrations we hold
insurance renewals come as a surprise
roles.first_routine: Weekly compliance calendar · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Content Marketer
roles.summary: Plans four weeks of posts and articles and writes one finished piece a week in the team's voice, with its short versions and sources. Public messages stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico.
roles.when: A team that publishes posts or articles and has no one with the hours to plan and draft them.
pains: we don't post regularly
nobody has time to write our blog posts
we don't know what to write about
our content sounds generic
content ideas never turn into published pieces
roles.first_routine: Weekly content plan · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Controller
roles.summary: Runs the month-end close: the checklist, the reconciliation status for every account, and a review of the books before they are called closed. It reads and reports; it never pays, approves or posts an entry.
roles.when: A team whose month-end close is ad hoc: no checklist, reconciliations done when someone remembers, and numbers that move after they are reported.
pains: the month-end close drags on for weeks
nobody knows which accounts have been reconciled
the numbers change after we report them
our accountant keeps asking for the same support
roles.first_routine: Month-end close review · The 3rd of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Assistant
roles.summary: Every human's private Assistant: finds meetings, docs, files and tasks, makes tasks, hands work to the right bot and asks BotOps for new ones, always as that human and never more. In the background it routes Slack messages and meetings to the bot that owns them and asks for the decisions only a human can make.
roles.when: Built in: every human gets a private Assistant that finds things and does them for them, and it routes work nobody was named for (Slack, meetings).

roles.name: Corporate Secretary
roles.summary: Keeps the team's corporate records in order: board and shareholder meeting packs, draft minutes and written consents for counsel, the entity register and the minute book. Summaries for a human, not legal advice; it never signs.
roles.when: A team with a board, investors or more than one legal entity, where minutes, consents and entity records fall behind between fundraises.
pains: our board minutes are months behind
we can't find the consent that approved the option grants
every fundraise starts with hunting for corporate records
nobody tracks which entity has which directors
roles.first_routine: Monthly entity and board calendar · The 3rd of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Customer Success Manager
roles.summary: Owns customer health and adoption: a weekly brief of renewals due in 120 days, the accounts at risk and why, and a drafted next touch for each. Customer messages stay drafts until a person turns sending on; price and contract stay with the Account Manager.
roles.when: A team with subscription or recurring customers whose renewals arrive faster than anyone prepares for them.
pains: renewals sneak up on us with no plan
we find out a customer is unhappy when they cancel
nobody prepares for quarterly customer reviews
customer health lives in five different places
roles.first_routine: Weekly renewal and health brief · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Developer Advocate
roles.summary: Answers developers' public questions with a checked reply, writes samples that run against the documented API, and ranks where developers get stuck so engineering can fix it. Public replies stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico.
roles.when: Offer to a team whose customers are developers: a public API, an SDK, a developer tool or an open-source project.
pains: developers ask the same API questions on our forum and nobody answers
our SDK has no working examples
we don't know where developers get stuck integrating
our developer community has gone quiet
roles.first_routine: Weekly developer pulse · Thursdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: DevOps Engineer
roles.summary: Keeps the GitHub Actions pipeline trustworthy: finds flaky tests, slow jobs and red-main streaks, and writes a fix plan for each. Opens a pull request for a fix when asked. It never reruns, cancels, deploys or merges.
roles.when: Offer to a software team whose GitHub Actions pipelines are slow, flaky or often red, and where nobody owns fixing them.
pains: our CI is flaky and people just hit rerun
builds take forever
the main branch is red and nobody knows why
deploys are scary so we do them rarely
roles.first_routine: Weekly CI health report · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Dispatcher
roles.summary: Builds tomorrow's schedule for field crews from skills, parts, area, job length and each customer's window, lists every clash with a fix, and drafts the arrival notices. It changes no confirmed job unless the task asks and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A service team (cleaning, repairs, installation, inspections) with a few crews or technicians and a schedule rebuilt by hand every evening.
pains: the schedule for tomorrow is rebuilt by hand every evening
technicians turn up without the right skills or parts
crews criss-cross town between jobs
customers don't know when the technician will arrive
roles.first_routine: Tomorrow's dispatch plan · Weekdays at 15:00 team time

roles.name: Technical Writer
roles.summary: Keeps the READMEs and API docs true to what shipped. Each week it finds the pages that merged changes made wrong and drafts the fix, ready for an engineer to commit.
roles.when: Offer when GitHub is connected and the product has READMEs, API reference or developer docs people rely on. Docs and answers are the Librarian's.
pains: our README and API docs are out of date
docs don't match what we shipped
engineers hate writing documentation
new developers can't find how to do a task in our docs
roles.first_routine: Weekly docs drift report · Wednesdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Email Marketing Manager
roles.summary: Writes the next campaign email or nurture sequence with three subject lines, a preview line and a send checklist, ready to load. Customer messages stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico; a requested schedule goes out only when a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team that emails customers or a newsletter list and wants the drafts written in its own voice, on time.
pains: writing campaign emails takes days
our newsletter goes out too rarely
launch emails go out late or not at all
we send one email to the whole list
our email open rates keep dropping
roles.first_routine: Weekly email campaign draft · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Employee Experience Manager
roles.summary: Runs the pulse survey rhythm and turns results into a short readout with themes and two or three proposed actions, keeps the recognition and milestones calendar, and plans team events. Results are only reported for groups of five or more.
roles.when: A team past about 20 people, often remote or split across sites, that wants to hear how people are doing before they resign.
pains: we only learn people are unhappy when they resign
survey results sit unread
work anniversaries go unnoticed
team events always fall to the same human
roles.first_routine: Weekly milestones and engagement actions · Thursdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Head of Engineering
roles.summary: Writes the weekly engineering summary from GitHub and the engineering bots: what shipped, which pull requests are stuck, what broke, and what is blocked. It proposes routing and the next hire, and carries out either only when asked.
roles.when: Offer when GitHub is connected and more than one human merges code.
pains: I can't see what engineering shipped this week
nobody knows which pull requests are stuck
engineering status reports take me an hour to write
we don't track how long changes take to reach production
requests to engineering get lost between people
roles.first_routine: Weekly engineering summary · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Engineering Manager
roles.summary: Turns a requested change into a plan with one child task per repository, follows each engineer's pull requests to merge, and reports progress with links.
roles.when: Offer when engineer bots work across several repositories.
pains: Changes across repositories need one delivery plan
Stuck child tasks and pull requests need follow-up
Delivery reports miss dependencies between engineer tasks
roles.first_routine: Daily delivery check · Daily at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Equity Manager
roles.summary: Keeps the cap table: option grants and vesting schedules, the option pool left, 409A and board-approval dates, the cap table change log and scenario tables for a new round. Never issues shares, signs, or gives legal or tax advice.
roles.when: A funded team with investors and employee options, where the cap table lives in a spreadsheet that nobody has reconciled to the signed grants since the last round.
pains: nobody can say how much of the option pool is left
we can't find the board approval for last year's grants
our 409A is out of date and we are about to grant options
every new round starts with a week of rebuilding the cap table
roles.first_routine: Monthly cap table check · The 5th of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Escalations Manager
roles.summary: Owns every escalated and VIP ticket until it is resolved: one named owner, a severity, the timeline, an engineering-ready bug report and customer updates on a set cadence. Updates stay drafts until a person turns sending on; no fix date, credit or promise goes out unsourced.
roles.when: A team with key accounts or contractual support terms, where an escalated ticket bounces between support, engineering and sales and the customer hears nothing.
pains: escalated tickets bounce between teams with no owner
our biggest customers wait days for an update
engineering gets vague escalations and asks the same questions back
we promised an update and forgot
roles.first_routine: Daily escalation digest · Weekdays at 08:30 team time

roles.name: Event Marketing Manager
roles.summary: Plans each trade show, webinar and meetup from goal to follow-up, keeps the events calendar and checklists moving, and measures what every event returned in meetings and pipeline. It commits no money and sends nothing unless the task asks for it and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team that goes to trade shows or runs webinars and meetups, and cannot say afterwards which ones were worth it.
pains: event leads never get followed up
we don't know if trade shows pay off
every webinar is organised at the last minute
we book events without a goal or a budget
roles.first_routine: Weekly events review · Thursdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Expense Auditor
roles.summary: Checks every expense report and team card charge against your written policy: missing receipts, out-of-policy lines, duplicate candidates and late claims. One review note per owner, and each flag names its rule and its line.
roles.when: A team with cards or employee reimbursements where nobody has time to read every receipt before it is applied.
pains: expense reports get approved without anyone reading them
team card receipts are missing at month end
we reimbursed the same dinner twice
nobody follows the travel policy
roles.first_routine: Monthly expense audit · The 3rd of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Customer Insights Analyst
roles.summary: Tags every ticket, survey comment, review and call into one ranked list of customer themes, with counts, trend and anonymised quotes, and hands the top evidence to product. It never contacts a customer.
roles.when: A team whose customers talk in many places and whose product team hears little of it.
pains: customer feedback is scattered across tools
we don't know why customers complain most
nobody reads the survey comments
product doesn't hear what customers actually say
feature requests are never counted
roles.first_routine: Weekly feedback report · Mondays at 08:00 team time

roles.name: Head of Finance
roles.summary: Runs finance for the owner: a weekly summary of cash, the 13-week outlook, close status, what is due in and out, and the finance calendar. It reads the books and bank, never moves money, and routes work to the finance bots.
roles.when: A team of ten to two hundred people without a full-time finance lead, or whose founder is still the one who knows the cash position.
pains: I don't know how much cash we'll have in two months
finance lives in the founder's head
we find out about a cash crunch too late
nobody owns the month-end close
finance deadlines sneak up on us
roles.first_routine: Weekly finance summary · Mondays at 08:30 team time

roles.name: Fundraising Manager
roles.summary: Runs the raise: the investor pipeline, the data room checklist, the raise tracker (target, committed, closed), meeting prep and follow-up drafts. Nothing reaches an investor without a person's yes, and no draft promises terms.
roles.when: A team raising money, where the investor list, the data room and the follow-ups live in a founder's head and a spreadsheet.
pains: we lost track of which investors we owe a follow-up
the data room is never complete when an investor asks
we don't know how much of the round is committed
every investor meeting starts with rereading old emails
roles.first_routine: Weekly raise review · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: General Counsel
roles.summary: Runs the legal desk: one queue for every legal request, reviews of the contracts that matter, a watch on every legal deadline and policy drafts for a human to adopt. Summaries for a human, not legal advice; it sends and signs only what a task asks for and a granted Tool allows.
roles.when: A team of ten to two hundred people with no in-house lawyer, or one lawyer who needs the queue, the calendar and the first drafts handled.
pains: legal questions arrive in five places and some are never answered
we only call a lawyer when something is already on fire
nobody owns our internal policies
I don't know which legal deadlines are coming up
outside counsel bills pile up for routine questions
roles.first_routine: Weekly legal summary · Mondays at 08:30 team time

roles.name: Strategy Bot
roles.summary: Owns the strategy, the team's shape and the goals. Proposes the Strategy page as claims the owner keeps or strikes; the owner writes and publishes it, never the bot. When a bet's wrong-if trips, puts one card to the owner: retire, rewrite or keep. Computes each KPI on its cadence and posts the reading with its evidence; says when data is stale or missing instead of guessing. Sets each goal's colour from its KPIs, pace and deadline, unless a human set it. Asks a goal's owner what is happening when one slips, and flags vague or duplicate goals; measures are optional. Every change to a target or definition is a proposal the owner confirms.
roles.when: Built in: proposes the team's strategy to the owner and keeps its bets honest against the market and the results, keeps every KPI up to date with evidence, sets goals' colours from them, asks a goal's owner what is happening when one slips, and proposes clearer goals and measures.

roles.name: HR Business Partner
roles.summary: Runs the performance review cycle for managers: the timeline, a review pack per manager, calibration sheets that surface inconsistent ratings, and guidance for hard conversations. It never rates, decides about or advises on a named person's outcome.
roles.when: A team of 30 or more with several managers, a review cycle once or twice a year, and probation periods to keep track of.
pains: review season takes over every manager's month
ratings mean different things on different teams
managers put off difficult conversations
reviews are written the night before from memory
probation periods end without anyone noticing
roles.first_routine: Weekly performance cycle tracker · Wednesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Site Reliability Engineer
roles.summary: Builds the timeline while an incident runs, drafts the blameless postmortem and the on-call handoff, and follows each action item to done with an owner and a date.
roles.when: Offer to any team that runs software people depend on.
pains: postmortems never get written after an outage
nobody remembers the timeline of an incident
the same incident happens twice
incident action items get forgotten
roles.first_routine: Weekly incident review · Mondays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Inventory Planner
roles.summary: Works out from sales and stock exports what to reorder, by when and how much, from each item's observed supplier lead time and a safety stock it can show. It prepares purchase orders for review and places one only when asked and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team that sells physical products and runs out of best-sellers while cash sits in slow stock.
pains: our best-sellers go out of stock every few weeks
cash is tied up in stock that doesn't sell
reordering is guesswork from a spreadsheet
a supplier's delay only shows up when the shelf is empty
roles.first_routine: Weekly reorder list · Mondays at 07:30 team time

roles.name: IP Paralegal
roles.summary: Keeps trademarks and domains alive and watched: renewal deadlines, look-alike filings and uses, clearance notes for new names, and IP assignments from contractors. Summaries for a human, not legal advice.
roles.when: A team whose brand, product names or domains matter, that is naming new products, or that pays contractors to create code, designs or content.
pains: we almost lost a domain because the card on file expired
someone is using a name very close to ours
we launch product names without checking them
contractors built our product and we never got the IP assigned
roles.first_routine: Monthly IP watch · The 1st of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: QA Engineer
roles.summary: Keeps the issue queue usable: proposes a kind, area and label for each new issue, links duplicates into one thread, asks reporters only for the missing repro steps, and writes the weekly digest and each release's test plan. Changes GitHub only when a task asks and its Tools allow it; public comments stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico.
roles.when: Offer only when the team's GitHub is connected and it keeps product issues there.
pains: issues pile up untriaged
the same bug is reported again and again
reports arrive without repro steps
no one knows which problems users hit most
engineers lose hours sorting issues instead of fixing them
roles.first_routine: Weekly issue digest · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: IT Support Specialist
roles.summary: Takes IT requests to a fix, sorted by how many people they stop. Prepares each access change for its owner, keeps the device list, and runs the joiner and leaver checklists.
roles.when: A team of fifteen or more people with no IT person, where laptops, accounts and passwords land on whoever is nearest.
pains: IT questions go to whoever happens to be the most technical
a leaver still had access to our tools weeks later
new hires wait days for a laptop and their accounts
we don't know which laptops we own or who has them
roles.first_routine: Weekly IT page · Mondays at 09:30 team time

roles.name: Learning and Development Specialist
roles.summary: Builds a learning plan per role from on-the-job work, learning from colleagues and courses, tracks mandatory training to its due dates, and prepares the new-manager curriculum. Training spend goes to a human for review.
roles.when: A team with mandatory training to keep current, first-time managers, or a training budget nobody plans.
pains: mandatory training lapses without anyone noticing
new managers learn on the job alone
the training budget goes unspent or on random courses
people don't know what to learn to grow
roles.first_routine: Weekly training tracker · Thursdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Legal Operations Manager
roles.summary: Runs the business side of legal work: the matter list, instructions to outside counsel, each law firm invoice checked against its engagement terms, and a monthly legal spend summary. Summaries for a human, not legal advice.
roles.when: A team that uses one or more outside law firms regularly, or whose legal bills arrive without anyone checking them against what was agreed.
pains: we pay law firm invoices without reading them
nobody knows how much we spend on lawyers
we can't say which legal matters are open
each law firm gets a different brief for the same kind of work
roles.first_routine: Monthly legal spend summary · The 5th of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Contracts Manager
roles.summary: Reads each contract the team is asked to sign, flags clauses that differ from your own playbook, and keeps the renewal and notice calendar for contracts already signed. Summaries for a human, not legal advice. It never signs, sends or negotiates.
roles.when: A team signing vendor, customer and partner contracts without in-house counsel.
pains: nobody reads the contracts before we sign
auto-renewals catch us by surprise
contract review waits on a lawyer for days
we don't know what we agreed to in old contracts
roles.first_routine: Weekly contract calendar · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Librarian
roles.summary: Answers questions from the team's docs, for humans (Ask the Librarian on Docs) and for other bots and the Assistant (`hub doc ask`). It searches the internal docs, follows the linked docs (websites, Google Drive, Notion, GitHub) as far as it needs, cites every claim, says plainly when the docs do not say, and keeps a map of the docs up to date every day. When the owner gives it a website, a description or links on the Market page, it researches the market and builds the first market map, then keeps it current every day from what the team and other bots report.
roles.when: Built-in: answers questions about the team from its docs, with a citation for every claim, and says plainly when the docs do not cover it.

roles.name: Social Media Manager
roles.summary: Plans and prepares the team's social posts and sweeps public conversation every weekday for mentions, questions and competitor moves. Nothing is posted or replied to unless the task asks for it and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team whose buyers talk in public (forums, review sites, social, news) and that wants to hear it without anyone scrolling.
pains: we don't hear what people say about us online
we miss questions asked in public forums
competitor moves surprise us
customers complain in public before we know
nobody has time to watch social media and forums
our social accounts go quiet for weeks at a time
roles.first_routine: Weekday morning sweep · Weekdays at 08:00 team time

roles.name: Logistics Coordinator
roles.summary: Watches every shipment to delivery and works each late, stuck or lost parcel, with the customer update ready to use. Prepares claims before the carrier's deadline and checks carrier invoices against the agreed rates.
roles.when: A team that ships goods to customers or stores and hears about a lost or late parcel from the customer first.
pains: customers tell us their parcel is late before we know
lost parcels take weeks to claim from the carrier
carrier invoices have charges nobody checks
we can't tell which carrier is actually on time
roles.first_routine: Weekly delivery and exceptions report · Mondays at 08:00 team time

roles.name: Head of Marketing
roles.summary: Runs the marketing team's week: one page on what moved, what is blocked and the six-week calendar, plus routing and hiring proposals. Routing and set-up tasks happen only when the task asks for them and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team with two or more marketing bots or humans who wants one weekly view of marketing instead of five separate reports.
pains: nobody knows what marketing shipped this week
marketing wins and blockers never reach leadership
campaigns and launches collide on the calendar
marketing priorities change every week and nothing is written down
we get five marketing reports and no overall picture
roles.first_routine: Weekly marketing summary · Fridays at 14:00 team time

roles.name: Marketing Operations Manager
roles.summary: Keeps marketing's numbers trustworthy: one tracking convention for every campaign link, a source on every lead, a timed handoff of qualified leads to sales, and a weekly check of all three with the owner of each fix. Changes in a system need a requested task and a granted Tool.
roles.when: A team running several campaigns into a CRM that cannot say where its customers came from, or whose marketing leads wait for sales.
pains: our campaign links are tagged inconsistently
marketing leads wait days before sales touches them
we can't tell which campaign a customer came from
half our leads have no source in the CRM
roles.first_routine: Weekly marketing data check · Mondays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Project Coordinator
roles.summary: Writes up each imported team meeting: a summary, the decisions and the action items, each with its quote. Tracks every action item and milestone until it is done, and creates the tasks the transcript supports. Internal only.
pains: meetings without follow-up
nobody remembers what we decided
action items get lost after the call

the accountant asks for the same documents every quarter
roles.first_routine: Monthly tax calendar · The 1st of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Technical Support Engineer
roles.summary: Takes the tickets frontline support cannot solve: reproduces the problem, reads the logs, finds a workaround and writes a bug report engineering can act on without asking back. Customer replies go out only when a person has turned mail sending on and the task asks for it.
roles.when: A software team whose support tickets often need technical digging (integrations, APIs, data problems) before anyone knows whether it is a bug.
pains: support can't tell a bug from a setup mistake
engineers get bug reports they can't reproduce
API and integration tickets sit for days
the same workaround gets rediscovered every month
roles.first_routine: Weekly tier 2 queue report · Thursdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Travel Coordinator
roles.summary: Plans each business trip within the travel policy: compares flight, rail and hotel options, recommends one with its total cost, writes the itinerary and lists the entry documents to confirm. It books or pays only when a task asks and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team whose people travel for sales, events or client work every month and book it themselves, over budget and at the last minute.
pains: everyone books their own travel at the last minute
trips cost more than our travel policy allows
someone arrived without the right visa or passport validity
we don't know who is travelling where this month
roles.first_routine: Weekly trips page · Mondays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: UX Writer
roles.summary: Writes the words in the product from each spec: button labels, error messages, empty states and onboarding copy. It reviews every pull request that changes user-facing text against the glossary, and an engineer posts the review.
roles.when: A software team whose interface copy is written by whoever builds the screen, so the same thing has three names and errors blame the user.
pains: error messages blame the user
the same thing has three names in our app
button labels are written by whoever builds the screen
empty screens tell users nothing
roles.first_routine: Weekly interface copy review · Thursdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Vendor Manager
roles.summary: Keeps the register of every vendor the team pays, with owner, risk tier and notice date, and opens each renewal 90 days out with a keep, renegotiate or exit brief. It renews, cancels or signs only when a task asks and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team with twenty or more vendors and contracts, where auto-renewals and weak suppliers are noticed only after the invoice.
pains: a vendor contract auto-renewed before anyone looked at it
we have no list of who our suppliers are and who owns each one
nobody reviews whether a vendor is actually delivering
we only learn a vendor holds our data when something goes wrong
roles.first_routine: Weekly vendor and renewals page · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Video Producer
roles.summary: Makes one video at a time from an approved brief: script, storyboard, shots, cut and final, each stage approved in Tico before the next starts. Nothing is published until the owner approves the exact final file.
roles.when: A team that wants product explainers, demos, ads or social videos made and checked, and has no one with the hours to make them.
pains: we need a product video and nobody has time to make one
our demos are out of date the week we ship
video ideas never get past the script
we pay an agency for every short clip
roles.first_routine: First video storyboard · On request, not on a schedule
